title: Key points on the governance of patient navigators
summary:
The German health and social care system has complex regulations that can lead to patients receiving either too much or too little care. Often, the different regional requirements and the individual needs of patients are not sufficiently taken into account. Patient navigators act as guides, supporting people with medical needs by coordinating their care. For example, the patient navigator support patients during their stay in hospital and with further care. Previous projects have focused on implementing this concept into practice, but there is a lack of clear framework conditions and sufficient financing, especially at local level. LEX LOTSEN OWL (LLO) is addressing this by testing various ways various ways in which patient guides can be introduced and expanded in Germany. Specific recommendations are being developed for the necessary regulations.

The randomized controlled trial is investigating whether the accompaniment of patients by navigators can improve the quality of their care. Some patients are supported by a navigator (intervention arm), while others are randomly selected and do not receive navigator support (control arm). Patients with a stroke and cardiology patients can take part in the study.
 
The study has two main objectives:
1) To examine whether the quality of care for patients with navigator support increases compared to those without such support.
2) To develop recommendations for the introduction and expansion of this navigator concept within the German healthcare system. This involves addressing implementation issues and legal regulations.

The study examines the following primary hypotheses:
1) Hypotheis: The establishment of navigator offices increases relational coordination in the catchment area.
2) Hypothesis: The coordinated navigator activities increases the perceived quality of care experienced by patients with navigator support compared to patients without navigator support.
conditions: ICD-10-GM-2024: Acute ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke (I60-I64) or transient ischemic attack (G45); Acute ischemic heart disease (I20-I25), Paroxysmal tachycardia (I47), Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter (I48), Other cardiac arrhythmias (I49), Heart failure (I50)

interventions.name: Intervention group: Patients with navigator support i.e., navigated patients, for 12 months.
Control group: Patients without navigator support i.e., non-navigated patients, for 12 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Stroke navigators 
• Patients with confirmed stroke, ICD codes I60 - I64 and G45 (TIA)
• Continuous membership with a health insurance company participating in the LEX LOTSEN OWL project (consortium partner and cooperation partner health insurance companies).
• Written informed consent
• Patient's residence within the catchment area of the responsible patient navigator provider
• No existing care level or existing care level 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4 before the current stroke, or care level 5 initiated by a stroke
• Good German language skills or the guarantee of language support available for the duration of the intervention in order to understand and give informed consent to the declaration of consent

2) Cardio navigators
• Patients with confirmed diagnoses of ICD codes I20 - I25, I47 - I49, I50
• Continuous membership with a health insurance company participating in the LEX LOTSEN OWL project (consortium partner and cooperation partner health insurance companies)
• Written informed consent
• Patient's residence within the catchment area of the responsible patient navigator provider
• No existing care level or existing care levels 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4
• Good German language skills or the guarantee of language support available for the duration of the intervention in order to understand and give informed consent to the declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
1) Stroke navigators 
• Insured persons under the age of 18
• Insured persons residing outside the catchment area
• Existing care level 5 before the initial stroke
• Existing long-term inpatient care or long-term inpatient therapy prior to the current stroke
• Navigator level 0 (determined by navigators as part of the screening)
• Navigator levels 1-3, but with overlapping secondary diagnoses that require focus on another indication-specific field of network activity (determined by navigators as part of the screening), e.g., oncology, palliative care, dementia, psychiatry, geriatrics

2) Cardio navigators
• Insured persons under the age of 18
• Insured persons residing outside the catchment area
• Existing care level 5
• Existing long-term inpatient care or long-term inpatient therapy prior to the current cardiac event
• Navigator level 0 (determined by navigators as part of the screening)
• Navigator levels 1-3, but with overlapping secondary diagnoses that require focus on another indication-specific field of network activity (determined by navigators as part of the screening), e.g., oncology, palliative care, dementia, psychiatry, geriatrics
